decisions.decision: Loaded Vibes is optimized for generator UX, user time saved, and product-fit rather than governance or validation breadth.
CLI, web configurator, and loadedvibes.json share one recipe core.
Vibes remains the upstream SaaS template/reference; Loaded Vibes packages a self-contained derivative for generation.
Initial web configurator is stateless and requires no Loaded Vibes user account or database.

The self-contained Vibes derivative is composed from a stable golden baseline plus explicit marketing, sample-domain, and Stripe Connect overlays; presentation-only onboarding and admin examples are not promoted to production modules.
Generated identity and design choices are exposed through one typed product contract and consumed only by metadata, brand, semantic token, density, and navigation-shell surfaces.
Post-generation add is limited to packaged repository modules, preflights every file, and permits declared replacements only while the destination still matches the golden baseline.
Doctor performs only local metadata, dependency, Prisma-client, and non-secret environment-shape checks; explain derives product meaning and remaining setup from the manifest and recipe.
The stateless configurator imports the browser-safe shared recipe resolver, persists no server data, and exports the same normalized loadedvibes.json contract consumed by the CLI.

Web previews are representative Vibes-aligned surface mockups bound to normalized recipe fields; unsupported capability surfaces are labeled as excluded instead of simulated as working product behavior.
The canonical command is loaded-vibes create; the create-loaded-vibes package and legacy positional invocation remain compatible during the package-name transition.

Loaded Vibes is the sole owner and maintenance authority for one repository-local maximal white-label Hipster Stack template. DevNotes defines its engineering doctrine; no external application repository is an upstream, reference, synchronization source, or provenance dependency. Existing repository-local modules remain compatibility overlays until explicit retain-or-remove composition replaces them.
